problem: Prior modular waypoint-based VLN-CE agents (CWP, Sim2Sim, Reborn) plan only over local, nearby candidate waypoints. Backtracking to a distant location therefore takes several plan–control cycles, which accumulates error. Waypoint-predictor input choices (RGB vs depth) had not been studied. Existing controllers (heuristic, FMM, learned PointGoal) are not robust to obstacles, and when sliding along walls is forbidden (RxR-CE) they deadlock.
motivation: VLN-CE is far harder than graph-based VLN; success rates were under half of discrete-VLN results. Prior topological-map VLN methods needed a predefined nav-graph or environment pre-exploration (e.g., CMTP), which is unavailable in realistic settings. The authors observe two things. An online topological map built from predicted waypoints can give global structure for long-range planning and self-correction. In a sliding-forbidden setting with a larger chassis, a plain controller causes the agent to get stuck frequently, and this can collapse performance.
key_idea: Build a topological map online by self-organizing depth-only predicted waypoints into visited, current and ghost nodes. A cross-modal graph transformer with graph-aware self-attention picks a global long-term goal node over this map. The Dijkstra path to that goal is executed by a rotate-then-forward controller with a trial-and-error 'Tryout' escape heuristic for obstacle deadlocks.
insight:
Global planning over all observed ghost nodes beats local planning over adjacent nodes (57.21 vs 53.92 SR on R2R-CE val-unseen, Tab. 6) because it enables one-shot backtracking and self-correction. Graph-aware self-attention adds about 1 SR and helps global planning more (+1.24) than local (+0.77). For waypoint prediction, depth-only is best: 84.05 %Open and 57.21 SR, vs RGBD at 56.44 SR and RGB-only at 51.66 SR (Tab. 5), suggesting RGB semantics overfit to seen scenes when the task is only inferring accessibility. Map construction details matter:
- Deleting the selected ghost node before moving to it prevents endlessly re-selecting unreachable goals; removing it costs 4.80 SR.
- Averaging (accumulating) waypoints into ghost nodes is worth 1.32 SR.
- The merge threshold γ=0.5 m is best; γ=1.0 m yields too few nodes and costs about 12 SR.

Pre-training (MLM+SAP) is essential: 37.41 SR from scratch vs 57.21 with it. Pre-training on Habitat-rendered images beats MP3D images by about 2.7 SR due to the domain gap. On sliding-forbidden RxR-CE, the RF controller without Tryout collapses to 18.64 SDTW. Tryout restores it to 45.33, close to the teleportation upper bound of 46.04 and above learned PointGoal (43.79). FMM without a collision map fails (21.73 SDTW).
method: Depth-only waypoint predictor: CWP-style transformer (linear fusion of 12-view depth features and orientation, 2-layer transformer, MLP heatmap, NMS) predicts K nearby waypoint relative poses; pre-trained on the MP3D graph dataset of Hong et al. and frozen.

Node features: frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB and frozen DD-PPO PointGoal ResNet-50 depth features plus (cos,sin) heading are fused and passed through a trainable 2-layer panorama transformer. The current node is the mean of the 12 view embeddings; each waypoint takes the embedding of the view whose 30° sector contains it.

Online graph update via Waypoint Localization F_L (Euclidean nearest node, threshold γ=0.5 m): (1) a waypoint that hits a visited node is dropped and an edge is added; (2) one that hits a ghost node is accumulated and position/feature averaged; (3) otherwise it becomes a new ghost node. Edges store Euclidean distances.

Cross-modal planner: 9-layer text encoder and 4-layer LXMERT-style cross-modal graph encoder (hidden 768). Node encodings add pose (relative orientation and distance to current node) and last-visited-step encodings, plus a 'stop' node. Graph-aware self-attention adds E·W_e to the attention logits, where E holds all-pair shortest-path distances. An FFN scores ghost nodes and stop (visited and current nodes masked), and Dijkstra's algorithm gives a subgoal path to the chosen goal.

Control: the rotate-then-forward (RF) controller quantizes (Δθ, Δρ) into ROTATE 15° and FORWARD 0.25 m actions for each subgoal. The selected ghost node is deleted from the graph before execution to avoid re-selecting unreachable goals. 'Tryout' (sliding-forbidden only): if FORWARD does not change position, it tries 7 headings spaced from −90° to +90° with one FORWARD each, then restores the original heading.

Training: pre-training with MLM and single-action prediction (SAP) on offline topo maps derived from MP3D nav-graphs with Habitat-rendered RGB-D, 100k iterations, batch 64, lr 5e-5. Fine-tuning in Habitat uses a DAgger-like demonstrator: on R2R-CE, the ghost node geodesically nearest the goal; on RxR-CE, the one nearest the next unvisited reference subgoal. Scheduled sampling moves from teacher- to student-forcing (decay 0.75 every 3k iterations), 15k iterations, batch 16, lr 1e-5.
Inference: greedy goal-node selection; at most 15 planning steps on R2R-CE and 25 on RxR-CE.

setting.backbone: LXMERT-style cross-modal graph transformer (initialized from LXMERT for R2R-CE, RoBERTa for multilingual RxR-CE; fine-tuned) with frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB encoder, frozen DD-PPO ResNet-50 depth encoder, and frozen depth-only CWP waypoint predictor
setting.model_size: not stated (LXMERT-base config: 9 text / 2 panorama / 4 cross-modal layers, hidden 768)
setting.training_data: Pre-training on R2R and RxR discrete paths, with topo maps from MP3D nav-graphs and Habitat-rendered RGB-D, augmented with Prevalent and RxR-Marky (Marky-mT5) synthetic instructions. Fine-tuning online in Habitat on R2R-CE (10,819 instr.) / RxR-CE (60,300 instr.) train with DAgger-style supervision. Waypoint predictor pre-trained on the MP3D graph dataset (CWP).
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views at 30° intervals) + ground-truth pose
setting.action_space: high-level: select ghost node in online topo map; executed as low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / ROTATE 15° / STOP via rotate-then-forward controller
setting.privileged: ground-truth agent pose from simulator for mapping and control (no sensor/actuation noise)

numbers_note: R2R-CE val-seen/val-unseen appear rounded to integers in Table 2 and with decimals in Tables 3/5 (same default model); the decimal versions are used. R2R-CE test-unseen is printed only as integers. The chassis-radius analysis is given only in a figure (Fig. 4), without numbers. Reborn, the authors' earlier challenge entry, is labeled '(ours)' but is a separately published method and is excluded. The text quotes Reborn test SDTW as 38.43, while the table shows 38.42.
results: On R2R-CE, ETPNav reaches 57.21 SR / 49.15 SPL on val-unseen and 55 SR / 48 SPL on test-unseen. This beats CWP-RecBERT (44 SR val-unseen) by 13 SR and Sim2Sim (44 SR / 37 SPL test) by 11 SR / 11 SPL. It also beats DUET transplanted into the same pipeline (53.71 SR). On RxR-CE test-unseen it gets 51.21 SR / 41.30 SDTW vs CWP-RecBERT's 24.85 / 19.05, though its nDTW (54.11) is slightly below the Reborn challenge entry (55.43), which the authors attribute to backtracking. Tryout lifts RxR-CE val-unseen SDTW from 18.64 (RF without Tryout) to 45.33.
limitations: Relies on ground-truth pose from the simulator for mapping and control; sensor/actuation noise is not studied (left as future work) and there is no real-robot evaluation.
Global planning encourages backtracking, which can hurt path fidelity (nDTW lower than local-planning Reborn on RxR-CE test).

Ghost-node positions come from predicted waypoints that may be off the navmesh, handled only by heuristic deletion. Performance is sensitive to map hyperparameters (γ) and depends heavily on pre-training on MP3D nav-graph data.
